headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law

members.title: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law
members.lead: Norwegian committee recognises achievements of former UN rights chief who stood up against apartheid in South Africa Nobel peace prize – latest updates Former UN human rights chief Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, a judge on the international court of justice (ICJ), has won the Nobel peace prize. Pillay, 85, from South Africa, who is a judge with the international court of justice, was recognised for her efforts to promote peace and international law, said Jørgen Watne Frydnes, chair of the Norwegian Nobel committee. members.title: Nobel winner Pillay jokes about sharing prize with Trump
members.lead: This year's Nobel peace prize winner Navi Pillay joked that she might "share the prize" with US President Donald Trump if people kept applauding her. "If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump," Pillay said in a video posted to X by the Secretary General of Amnesty International. The video showed Pillay being applauded in Nuremberg after the announcement of the award. . She said that her first reaction to hearing the news was that it must be a joke. "Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this," the 85-year-old said, wanting to make sure it was true. South African judge Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay (85) won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday "for her efforts to promote peace and international law", the Norwegian Nobel Committee said. . Pillay mentioned her work heading the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza. "The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what's happening there as genocide," she said. . "One of the main reactions to that report is paying tribute to me for my courage. And you can imagine how surprised I was, why would you need courage to speak the truth?" she added. The prize comes with a gold medal, a diploma and a prize sum of $1.2 million. The award will be presented at a formal ceremony in Oslo on 10 December, as the day marks the death anniversary of the the prizes' creator, Swedish inventor and philanthropist Alfred Nobel.
